id_and_class.summary: Petar Kojdić, drawing on Kant, treats the empirical world as an interface: a boundary where a non-empirical ground becomes partly available to finite knowers. Consciousness is the capacity of an agent at that interface to lock onto, sustain, and integrate lawlike patterns so that a unified, intelligible world is present to it, which makes consciousness a condition of the world’s intelligibility rather than an add-on inside a ready-made physical world.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as Stabilizer of the World Interface

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a structural capacity: the ability of a finite agent to stabilize lawlike patterns at the interface so that a coherent world appears to it.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Physical objects are relatively stable patterns on the interface, and space and time are the ways finite cognition charts it. Consciousness is neither produced by these patterns nor their creator: it is world-involving but not world-creating.
conceptual_ground.emergence_type: Not applicable (Kojdić denies consciousness is a substance, an emergent property, or a computation; it is a structural capacity realized in degrees by organized systems)
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Subjective presence is the appearing of a unified world to an agent. Following Nagel, Kojdić holds that any account of reality that sidelines this presence leaves out what it is for a world to appear.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Kojdić avoids appeals to irreducible qualia and accounts for experience through the coherent presence of a world to an agent.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: A non-empirical ground (posited only so appearances are not self-grounding, and neither described positively nor causally active), the interface, finite agents, and lawlike patterns.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Transcendental and meta-theoretical reflection on what any adequate world-model requires. Which systems have the capacity is left to empirical science.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: The ground, the interface where it becomes partly available, stable patterns on that interface (ordinary objects), and agents whose consciousness integrates those patterns into a world.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: World-presence and unity of experience; agency; normativity
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Stabilizing resonance: consciousness locks onto and integrates lawlike patterns at the interface instead of merely registering isolated inputs.
mechanism_and_dynamics.dynamics_of_emergence: Consciousness is graded and fragile. Cognitive overload, affective disturbance, or social and institutional conditions that undermine shared intelligibility can disrupt its clarity, scope, and stability.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: At the interface, in certain organized systems able to sustain stable alignment with lawful structure. Consciousness is not everywhere.
mechanism_and_dynamics.causation_and_functional_role: Without conscious stabilization, empirical reality would lack unity, lawfulness, and experiential coherence for any subject.
mechanism_and_dynamics.integration_or_binding: Integrating lawlike patterns into one coherent world is the defining work of consciousness on this view.
core_claims_and_evidence: The right question is how a unified, law-governed, experientially coherent world is possible, not how consciousness arises inside a given physical world.
Empirical reality is an interface between a non-empirical ground and cognitive limitation, not a self-standing domain of objects.
Physicalist, functionalist, phenomenological, and dual-aspect theories each describe partial stabilizations of the same interface.
Ethical and social norms are conditions for keeping a shared interface legible, so degrading agency or mutual recognition damages the empirical world itself.

empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Kojdić leaves open which biological or artificial systems have the stabilizing capacity. Because the ground is neither described nor causally active, the theory offers a framing for other theories rather than a mechanism of its own.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Coherent as a regulative, non-dogmatic Kantian framework that rejects both reductive eliminativism and panpsychism. Its placement under materialism is uneasy, since it denies that empirical reality is self-standing.

AI_consciousness.rationale: Kojdić treats consciousness as a structural capacity that some organized systems realize, and leaves open as an empirical question whether artificial systems can.

meaning_and_purpose.rationale: Kojdić ties consciousness to moral and social normativity, but he leaves the non-empirical ground undescribed, so whether meaning reaches beyond human agents stays open.
